rationale: Every clinic will receive the triggers, the intervention changes how referral happens, and the outcomes can come from routine records, so a pragmatic stepped-wedge trial in the eight clinics answers the question under real conditions. Randomising the order in which pairs of clinics switch protects against the clinic differences a before-after comparison would carry, and period effects are modelled. Nothing was retrieved, so the design rests on the investigator's local facts and on stated assumptions rather than on appraised evidence.
alternatives: Before-after comparison across the centre (refused: changes in referral practice over time would be confounded with the triggers)
Parallel cluster trial with four clinics kept on usual care throughout (refused: the division agreed to triggers in all eight clinics, and a stepped rollout protects clinic capacity)
Individually randomised trial (refused: triggers act at the clinic level, and patients of the same oncologist would contaminate each other)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge cluster randomised trials
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial with patient-reported outcomes would add questionnaires that the constraints exclude for very unwell patients; routine outcomes answer the main question, and patient experience can be studied later in a small subset.

decision.statement: Narrow the proposal to one pragmatic stepped-wedge trial of opt-out automatic referral triggers in the eight clinics, with days alive and out of hospital in the 90 days after trigger eligibility as the single primary outcome and palliative care waiting time as a balancing measure, and do not start until the research ethics board has decided on consent for automatic referral.
decision.question: Should the centre test automatic palliative care referral triggers, and in what form?

criteria.text: Enough patients meet a trigger (about 120 a month) to give a useful estimate.
The palliative care clinic cannot absorb the extra referrals within the added nurse time.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board decision on the trial, including consent for opt-out automatic referral
Medical oncology division agreement to opt-out automatic referral in all eight clinics
gates.evidence: Division minutes MO-2026-09-10, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Triggers in two clinics only as a first step
decision.note: No ledger claim exists because both recorded searches returned no records; the decision rests on the confirmed empty searches and the investigator's local facts. The ethics gate stays unknown until the board decides.

summary: Pragmatic stepped-wedge trial recommended; the decision narrows the proposal to one primary outcome and waits for the ethics board.
